keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 189-210 (the former 189-196 and 197-210 keyframes merged); no Cliopatria row (the Han shape keeps Liang). 'Han Sui's group in Jincheng, Ma Teng's group in the Wei Valley'; the Han Sui page: the two 'declared themselves co-rulers of Liang Province'; the Ma Teng page: Liang Province 'covering parts of present-day Shaanxi and Gansu'. No frontier on any page. Reviewer fixes (ea-02-x-fixed): (1) the Guanzhong is gone. 'Yong' of the End of the Han page's 197 sentence ('Ma Teng and Han Sui, who controlled Yong and Liang provinces') is not the Wei valley: the Yong Province page has a Yongzhou Inspectorate set up in 194 over 'Wuwei, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Xihai ... west of the Liang River' (seat at Guzhang), and the Three Guardians joined Yongzhou only in 213; the Hexi is already inside Gansu. The Baoji circle stays for Ma Teng's Wei-valley group (the liang-province-rebels shape of 187-189 has it too). (2) Song Jian's Fuhan (Linxia 80 km, 189-214) is cut out of Gansu, so the ground is drawn once. (3) Ningxia is in from 189, as the rebels' shape (liang-province-rebels_187: Gansu, Ningxia and Baoji) passes to its successor. The Hanzhong 100 km circle of zhang-lu (194-215) is also cut out, because it clips the Qinling edge of the Baoji circle and Gansu's southern tip.

ledger.note: 197: Liang submits to the court. 'Cao Cao was able to persuade Ma Teng and Han Sui, who controlled Yong and Liang provinces' (End of the Han page, 197 paragraph); the Ma Teng page has the two 'pledged allegiance to the Han dynasty' after Zhong Yao brokered peace (undated), and the Han Sui page puts Zhong Yao's mission and Liang Province 'under Cao Cao's authority' in 200. Retyped from a gain of the Guanzhong (repair pass): the pages give no new land in 197, and 'Yong' of 194-213 was the Hexi commanderies (Yong Province page), already inside Gansu; the Three Guardians joined Yongzhou in 213. Land: the Liang of the keyframe.

ledger.note: 211: the Wei valley is lost. The End of the Han page: the coalition led by Ma Chao and Han Sui 'was defeated by Cao Cao at the Battle of Tong Pass in 211, and their territories were annexed by Cao over the next few years'; the Han Sui page: after Tong Pass he 'retreated once again to Liang Province' and Cao Cao captured and killed his children and grandchildren; Ma Teng page: Ma Chao 'remained behind in Liang Province with Han Sui'. Repair pass: the note used to quote 'Ma Chao and Han Sui held Liang and Yong until 211', which is not on the page (the 'who controlled' wording is in the sentence before, about the warlords' suspicions); the year stands. The Guanzhong is no longer the lost land: the pages give no Guanzhong holding, only Liang Province 'covering parts of present-day Shaanxi and Gansu' (Ma Teng page) and Cao Cao's fear of Ma Teng's 'influence in Guanzhong' (208), so only the Baoji circle goes at 211 and Gansu with Ningxia is annexed 'over the next few years' (dissolve 215).
211: the coalition is broken at Tong Pass; Han Sui and Ma Chao retreat to Liang Province.

notes:
Han Sui and Ma Teng, the Liang warlords 189-215. 4 pages opened (Han Sui, Ma Teng, Liang Province rebellion, End of the Han dynasty). No Cliopatria row; ea-02-c's han-dynasty has Cao Cao taking Liang and Yong in 211 and drops the Hexi etc. in 215.
Unsettled: (1) the extent of 'Yong' beyond Guanzhong and when the warlords held it; (2) the Han Sui and Ma Teng pages disagree with the End of the Han page on 197 (the Han Sui page puts the peace in 200 and has no 197 submission); (3) the 211-215 shape is a placeholder (confidence 1): Ma Chao's flight to Zhang Lu in Hanzhong (Zhang Lu page, after Tong Pass) and his later years are outside the pages' dates; (4) Ma Teng's execution is June or July 212 on his page (not 211); (5) Cao Cao's nominal overlordship of the two from 197 (End of the Han) and 200 (Han Sui) could be a vassal tie in cao-cao's dossier: not entered here.
Counterparts: han-dynasty, cao-cao exist; liang-province-rebels and song-jian are written by this batch.
Repair pass (ea-02-x-fixed): 5 pages now (Han Sui, Ma Teng, Liang Province rebellion, End of the Han dynasty, Yong Province), the budget for a state without a Cliopatria row; Ma Chao's page was not opened for the 211-215 shape (page budget). (1) The Guanzhong is removed from the 197 event and the keyframes: Yong Province of 194-213 was the Hexi (Yong Province page), no opened page gives Han Sui or Ma Teng the Wei valley beyond the Baoji circle, and the 197 event is a vassal_start to han-dynasty (ended by vassal_end 211/9). ea-02-c's han-dynasty /ledger/98 (196 loss of Yong to han-sui) and /ledger/103 (211 gain from han-sui) still use the old reading; they are ea-02-c's to fix. (2) The note that quoted 'Ma Chao and Han Sui held Liang and Yong until 211' is replaced by the page's wording, which sits in two sentences; the year 211 stands. (3) K0 and K1 merged (189-210) after the Guanzhong left; Fuhan (Linxia 80 km) is cut out of 189-215; Ningxia is in from 189. (4) The 211 loss is the Baoji circle only; Gansu and Ningxia are annexed 'over the next few years' (the Han Sui page puts his last stand in Liang Province, 215). The zhang-lu Hanzhong circle is cut from every han-sui shape as well (about 33 cells of overlap in the Qinling and Gansu's south tip).
